arguments.summary: Completed-session technical evidence is constructive for both stocks through 2026-10-02, but NVDA has the cleaner 63-session setup: stronger absolute return, materially positive excess versus both SPY and XLK, lower realized volatility and a shallower 63-session close-path drawdown. MU has a strong 21-session rebound and remains ahead over 63 sessions, but its five-session relative signs are negative, its 63-session XLK edge is only +0.3068 percentage points, and observed path risk is much higher. Historical regime frequencies are descriptive analogs, not calibrated probabilities.

claims.text: NVDA completed 2026-10-02 at a split-adjusted SIP close of $233.95. Its price returns were +3.9454% over 5 sessions, +4.2511% over 21 and +19.6369% over 63. The close was 4.54% above SMA20, 7.18% above SMA50 and 16.56% above SMA200; SMA20 rose 0.9161% over five sessions. The close was 1.3385% above the prior 21-session closing high, while last-session volume was 1.3382 times the prior-20-session median and five-session average volume was 1.1189 times that median. These measurements support absolute trend continuation, but a single elevated-volume observation is not sustained breakout confirmation.

PAIR NVDA/SPY 5=+4.1671 21=+3.6656 63=+17.1931
PAIR NVDA/XLK 5=+2.1418 21=-4.5778 63=+10.7902
On matched 2026-10-02 SIP, split-adjusted price-return windows, NVDA led SPY at 5, 21 and 63 sessions. Against XLK it led at 5 and 63 sessions but lagged over 21 sessions, so the recent absolute rise and new closing high did not produce leadership over the technology benchmark across every window.

NVDA's annualized realized volatility was 14.88%, 24.85% and 38.25% over the 5-, 21- and 63-session windows, respectively, and its maximum 63-session close-path drawdown was -10.5835%. Under the coarse current regime (close above SMA20, SMA20 above SMA50, positive 21-session return), overlapping historical observations had positive forward-return frequencies of 58.1132%/58.4906%/71.6981% at 5/21/63 sessions (n=265), versus unconditional rates of 58.8697%/61.6954%/73.4694% (n=637). Thus this particular regime did not improve the positive-return frequency over base rates in this finite lookback, despite positive medians; it should not be treated as a forecast.

NVDA's strongest continuation case is a rising short trend, a close above the prior 21-session high, positive 63-session leadership versus both SPY and XLK, and moderately elevated recent volume. The strongest opposing path is momentum exhaustion: RSI14 was 82.97, 21-session performance still lagged XLK by 4.5778 points, and the historical regime frequencies were not better than unconditional rates. A recent rebound can therefore coexist with an intermediate sector-relative lag; trend in the price level is not the same as leadership in every benchmark window.

MU completed 2026-10-02 at a split-adjusted SIP close of $1,074.89. Its price returns were -0.6828% over 5 sessions, +12.4268% over 21 and +9.1536% over 63. The close was 4.87% above SMA20, 12.43% above SMA50 and 57.70% above SMA200; SMA20 rose 3.1041% over five sessions. However, MU remained 2.0503% below its prior 21-session closing high. Last-session volume was 1.1404 times the prior-20-session median and five-session average volume was 1.2522 times that median, consistent with active participation but not proof of a breakout.

PAIR MU/SPY 5=-0.4611 21=+11.8413 63=+6.7098
PAIR MU/XLK 5=-2.4865 21=+3.5978 63=+0.3068
On matched 2026-10-02 SIP, split-adjusted price-return windows, MU lagged both SPY and XLK over five sessions but led both over 21 and 63 sessions. The 63-session lead over XLK was only +0.3068 percentage points, so medium-window sector leadership was marginal even though the 21-session rebound was strong.

MU's annualized realized volatility was 36.57%, 49.55% and 74.56% over the 5-, 21- and 63-session windows, respectively, and its maximum 63-session close-path drawdown was -25.4770%. Under the same coarse positive regime, overlapping historical observations had positive forward-return frequencies of 59.1503%/67.6471%/79.0850% at 5/21/63 sessions (n=306), versus unconditional rates of 57.9278%/63.4223%/71.1146% (n=637). The 63-session conditional sample nevertheless had a -15.9730% 10th-percentile return, illustrating that favorable historical frequency coexisted with material downside dispersion; these dependent observations are not calibrated probabilities.

MU's strongest continuation case is the steeply rising SMA20, double-digit 21-session gain, positive 21- and 63-session excess returns, and above-median recent volume. The strongest opposing path is that the rebound stalls below the prior 21-session high: five-session relative performance is already negative, the 63-session XLK edge is nearly flat, RSI14 was 74.88, and both realized volatility and drawdown show substantially greater path risk than NVDA. This is a rebound with fragile near-term leadership rather than uniform strength.

For the exact 63-session window ending 2026-10-02, NVDA is the stronger technical preference over MU: NVDA returned +19.6369% versus MU's +9.1536%, exceeded XLK by +10.7902 points versus MU's +0.3068, and had lower 63-session annualized realized volatility (38.25% versus 74.56%) and a shallower maximum close-path drawdown (-10.5835% versus -25.4770%). The competing explanation is horizon dependence: MU led NVDA in 21-session excess versus SPY (+11.8413 versus +3.6656), so a continued rebound could narrow the 63-session gap. This is a market-behavior comparison, not a fundamental or valuation judgment.

The market was closed at the assessment time, so completed closes—not current executable quotes—anchor this analysis. NVDA's IEX snapshot showed a last trade of $234 near the 2026-10-02 close but no latest quote. MU's IEX snapshot showed a $1,074.71 last trade and a $1,030.27/$1,141.62 bid/ask stamped around that close. IEX is single-venue coverage, and these stale market-closed observations do not establish consolidated executable prices.

gaps.description: Stronger continuation conviction requires subsequent completed-session OHLCV to test whether NVDA sustains the prior-high breakout and whether MU closes above its prior 21-session high; the supplied panel ends on 2026-10-02.

The empirical forward-return panels use overlapping observations from one finite 2023-12-18 to 2026-07-06 lookback and only three coarse regime signs. They do not provide independent samples, causal estimates, out-of-sample validation or calibrated probabilities.

assumptions: All return and relative-return comparisons use matched 2026-10-02 completed sessions, SIP feed, split-adjusted prices and price-return convention.
Moving-average thresholds are frozen values observed on 2026-10-02, not future dynamic averages and not execution levels.
Technical preference is limited to the 63-session mandate and does not incorporate business quality, valuation, policy or portfolio suitability.
arguments.counter_thesis: The technical ranking can reverse if MU's rebound clears its prior 21-session closing high and restores positive five-session excess while retaining positive 21- and 63-session XLK excess, or if NVDA loses its frozen SMA20 level and its 21-/63-session sector-relative excess turns negative. High RSI readings and the dependent analog samples caution against extrapolating either trend.

review_conditions.description: A completed SIP split-adjusted NVDA close below the frozen 2026-10-02 SMA20 level of 223.786 before expiry would weaken the short-trend continuation case and shift interpretation from breakout continuation to trend deterioration; this is a research checkpoint, not an order.

Recompute NVDA's matched 21- and 63-session excess returns versus XLK after subsequent completed sessions. If both signs become negative, invalidate sector-leadership support for the 63-session setup; if 21-session excess turns positive while 63-session excess remains positive for two consecutive completed sessions, treat leadership as broadening across windows.

A completed SIP split-adjusted MU close below the frozen 2026-10-02 SMA20 level of 1025.0015 before expiry would weaken the rebound setup and indicate that the steep recent average rise has not held; this is a research checkpoint, not an order.

Recompute MU's matched 5-, 21- and 63-session excess returns versus XLK after subsequent completed sessions. A negative 63-session sign would remove the current, marginal sector-leadership claim; confirmation requires five-session excess to turn positive while 21- and 63-session excess remain positive for two consecutive completed sessions.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Both are compared with the same dated XLK sector proxy. Their relative behavior can therefore reflect a shared technology-sector price move as well as stock-specific movement; the panel measures excess return but does not identify causality or portfolio weights.
shared_exposures.qualification: Completed-session price comparison only through 2026-10-02; not a claim about fundamental sector exposure or future co-movement.

agent_report.work_summary: I analyzed the supplied completed-session price, relative-return, technical-path and historical-regime panels for NVDA and MU. I checked all four benchmark pairs at 5, 21 and 63 sessions, separated completed SIP closes from market-closed IEX snapshot observations, and compared trend levels, volume ratios, realized volatility and close-path drawdowns.
main_conclusions: NVDA has the cleaner 63-session technical profile, with stronger return and excess return plus lower observed path risk than MU.
NVDA led SPY across all three windows but lagged XLK over 21 sessions, so its price breakout is not uniform sector leadership.
MU's 21-session rebound is strong, but five-session relative signs are negative and its 63-session XLK lead is only +0.3068 points.
Historical regime frequencies are descriptive and dependent; NVDA's regime did not beat unconditional positive-return base rates, while MU's did but retained wide downside dispersion.
agent_report.short_summary: Technically, NVDA is preferred for the exact 63-session window, while MU is a higher-volatility rebound whose sector-relative edge is fragile. Both views require confirmation from future completed sessions rather than stale single-venue snapshots.
limitations: No completed-session data later than 2026-10-02 were available.
Historical forward-return samples overlap and are not calibrated probabilities.
This role did not assess valuation, fundamentals, policy or execution suitability.
